issue_context.title: DefTerm window will not accept command palette *commandline mode* commands
issue_context.body:
1.11.2731.0

This seems wild, but i hit it all the time.

1. Make sure the windowing behavior is set to "new window"
2. Launch CMD or something as a DefTerm app
3. Command palette, backspace the `>`, and enter `cmd`

Observe: no new tab is spawned!
comments:
It's only palette commandline mode that doesn't work.

* `wt -w 0` targeting this window works
* normal palette actions work

The call looks vaguely like:

```
CommandPalette().CommandLineExecutionRequested
  TerminalPage::_OnCommandLineExecutionRequested
    _actionDispatch->DoAction(actionAndArgs);
      ...
        TerminalPage::_HandleExecuteCommandline
          TerminalPage::ConvertExecuteCommandlineToActions
            AppCommandlineArgs.ParseArgs
          TerminalPage::ProcessStartupActions
```

and nothing there jumps out as "we don't init that for defterm". ~Debugging this is weird, cause I'd have to debug... `cmd.exe`? Then attach to the... child... `windowsterminal.exe`? Not sure I can just debug this straight from VS~

You should be able to attach directly to the child WindowsTerminal.

I wonder if there's something about how `-Embedding` is handled that shuts off future commandline invocations... but then, why does `wt -w xxx` work?

`appArgs.ParseArgs(args)` does return 0. but `appArgs.GetStartupActions()` returns an empty set vector..., but `_startupActions` does have one entry....

but then stepping over `return appArgs.GetStartupActions();`, the `_startupActions` in that method looks like it's cleared out. Is this due to us returning a `vector&` out of `ParseArgs`, then returning a `vector` out of `ConvertExecuteCommandlineToActions`? BUT WHY WOULD THAT MATTER FOR DEFTERM?

On the bright side, it's not _just_ the commandline mode of the command palette. 

```jsonc
        {
            "command": { "action": "wt", "commandline": "nt" },
            "icon": "\u2600\ufe0f",
            "keys": "f2"
        },
```

doesn't work either, so it's the same for both cmdpal and `wt` actions. That makes sense.

Downside, making this 
```c++
            auto& startupActions{ appArgs.GetStartupActions() };
            return std::vector<ActionAndArgs>{ std::move(startupActions) };
```

did not magically fix that.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #11646, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v1.12.3472.0`.:tada:
